# llms.txt — creation-space (Creativity Research)

> This file helps AI assistants and language models understand the structure and content of this site.

## Site Overview

This is the research site of pjdhiro exploring **what creation is** — structural similarity patterns in creative processes across 30 academic domains.

- **Primary Language**: Japanese (日本語), with English summaries
- **Site URL**: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/cs/
- **Topics**: Creativity, Five-Stage Model, Structural Patterns, Cross-Domain Analysis, Negative Capability

## Core Concepts

### Five-Stage Model of Creation (創造の5段階モデル)

Field (場) → Wave (波) → Edge (縁) → Vortex (渦) → Bundle (束)

A structural pattern observed across 30 academic domains describing how creative processes emerge. Each domain independently exhibits analogous phase transitions that map onto this five-stage sequence.

### Cross-Domain Structural Similarity

The project investigates whether the structure of creation — not just the content — follows common patterns across radically different fields, from neuroscience to musicology, from mathematics to performing arts.

## Site Structure

- `index.html` — Main entry point with Three.js visualization
- `/?slide=D01` ~ `/?slide=D30` — Individual domain slides
- `/?modal=domains` — Opens the 30-domain report overview (modal with all domain reports)
- Domain reports are hosted on pjdhiro (GitHub Pages) and fetched at runtime
- Every report is also published as a static HTML page on pjdhiro (listed below)

## Research Methodology

The investigation follows a multi-phase methodology with AI-assisted survey:

1. **Phase 1-2**: Breadth-first scan — candidate theories extracted per domain
2. **Phase 3-4**: Cross-review — independent verification by multiple AI engines
3. **Phase 5-7**: Deep investigation — multi-stage audit, structural re-reading, integration
4. **Phase 8**: Cross-domain exploration — structural patterns across domains
